Q: Converting monetary values stored as strings into numeric values A:

This substring(total,2,2) can only handle, without error, data which is a correctly formatted numeric value starting with $, and is $10 or greater.

It can only accurately handle values between $10 and $99 with no cents (since you are stripping them off), and for any value greater than $99 you are removing all but the first two chars.

And this:

with total_revenue as (  
  select sum(cast(substring(total,2,2) as INT)) as converted_data
  from kap_sales
)
select converted_data
from total_revenue
limit 10;

Is attempting to sum every row in your table, because limit 10 is applied after the aggregation.

What this tells you is that you have data that doesn't match your assumptions.

Instead you should just remove the $ e.g. substring(total, 2, length(total)-1) i.e. keep the entire string after the $ rather than just 2 chars. Even simpler is right(total,length(total)-1).

And you should always go to the official source when trying to build a solution such as this: DB2 String Function Reference

Q: How to fix zsh: corrupt history file /home/mis/.zsh_history (Linux) A:

Just delete it with sudo rm ~/.zsh_history, then kill all your open terminals, e.g. pkill kitty

The sudo is probably not necessary, but this file is a bit weird about being deleted.

Q: Getting error while using fuzzywuzzy: UserWarning: Using slow pure-python SequenceMatcher. Install python-Levenshtein to remove this warning A:

if reinstalling python-Levenshtein does not fix the issue on Windows, the problem is usually missing Microsoft Visual C++ runtime.

Even when python-Levenshtein is installed, its DLL cannot load without the Visual C++ Redistributable. When this happens, fuzzywuzzy falls back to the slow pure-Python implementation and shows a warning.

Fix:
Install Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable 2015–2022 (x64) and try again.
